Builders window cleaning in Melbourne

The one trade on a handover with a clock running

Construction deposit on glass is not dust. Render run off, concrete slurry and cutting fines carry alkaline salts, and left on glazing through a few hot days and dew cycles they etch into the surface permanently. That turns a cleaning job into a glass replacement, a warranty claim and a delayed settlement.

  • Booked against your handover date
  • Etched glass is replacement, not cleaning
  • Film, stickers, silicone and fines
Get A Quote 0400 638 010
  1. Home
  2. Services

Why glass and not everything else

Because glass is the only exterior surface on a build where waiting makes the job impossible rather than just harder. Concrete slurry on a driveway left for six months needs acid instead of water. Deposit on glass left for six months may mean new glass.

The mechanism is simple. Cement based run off is alkaline. In contact with glass, with moisture and heat cycling it daily, it attacks the surface rather than sitting on it. The result is a permanent haze that does not change when the glass is wet, which is the test: if wetting it makes it disappear it is a deposit, and if it does not, it is etching and it is gone.

The timeline

What the same deposit becomes

Melbourne summer accelerates all of this considerably. A wet, cool month buys you time that a hot dry one does not.

The same render run off on the same window, at four points in time.
  State of the deposit What it takes Outcome
First week Still sitting on the surface Wash and a careful blade where needed Perfect, every time
First month Beginning to bond, especially in sun Treatment, dwell, then mechanical removal Normally perfect
One to three months Bonded, early surface attack starting Chemical treatment and repeated mechanical work Usually good. Some haze can remain
Beyond three months in summer Etched into the glass surface Nothing cleaning can do Replacement

Swipe for the rest of the columns

What comes off new glazing

Six things, in roughly this order

Protective film and stickers

Should come off well before handover. Baked through a Melbourne summer the adhesive transfers and, on powder coated frames, taking it off can take the finish with it.

Render and paint splatter

Spots and run marks. Removed by blade on glass, chemically on frames, which is why frames take longer than the glass does.

Concrete slurry and cutting fines

The alkaline one, and the reason for the clock. Fine, overall, and easy to mistake for ordinary dust until it will not wipe off.

Silicone and sealant smears

Needs solvent and a blade, carefully, because the wrong solvent attacks the glazing seal rather than the smear.

Tape residue and marker

Site marking on glass, which is routine and comes off easily when it is fresh.

Frames, tracks and sills

Where most of the time actually goes. Tracks full of site grit are what makes new windows feel wrong to an owner on day one.

Glass before scratch is a real risk, and it is handled by method

New glazing sometimes carries fabricating debris, small hard particles fused to the surface during manufacture. Blading glass without identifying those first is how windows get scratched during a builders clean, and it becomes an argument about who pays. The glass is inspected and tested before any blade is used, and where debris is present it is dealt with chemically instead.

Questions

Asked about new build glazing

When should builders window cleaning be booked?

Twice, ideally. Once when the wet trades have finished and the worst of the splatter is on, and again three to five days before handover for the final presentation.

If it is only going to happen once, make it the first one. Waiting until handover means the deposit has had the whole build programme to bond.

Is it really different from normal window cleaning?

Yes, in the method rather than the result. Normal glass is washed. Builders glass is assessed, treated, bladed where it is safe to and chemically worked where it is not, with the frames and tracks taking longer than the glass.

It is also considerably slower per window, which is why it is quoted as its own task rather than folded into a general tidy.

Can you remove the protective film?

Yes, and the sooner the better. Film left through a hot summer bakes on and the adhesive transfers to whatever it was protecting. On powder coated aluminium that can mean the removal takes the finish with it, so we will tell you if we think that is likely before starting.

What if the glass is already etched?

We will tell you before doing the work rather than after charging for it. The test is simple: wet the glass. A deposit disappears when wet, etching does not.

Etched glass cannot be cleaned back. The conversation at that point is about replacement and who wears it, which is exactly the conversation worth avoiding by booking the clean earlier.

Do you do volume work across an estate?

Yes, priced per lot rather than per visit, and sequenced against your handover dates. For a run of townhouses or an estate that is considerably cheaper and more reliable than a booking per house.

Exterior builders cleaning covers how the whole scope fits together.

Do you clean the inside of the glass too?

Where it is part of the scope and access allows, yes. On most builds the internal cleaner handles internal faces, which is why we keep the scopes separate and agree which of us is doing the inside at quote stage rather than on the day.
